dropped.item: Closing engagement question: 'What's worked for you in reducing no-shows?'
The author's stated lesson: 'sometimes the biggest operational wins come from meeting people where they already are'
Claim that closing the no-show gap matters for both the practice and the people it serves
'when they need it' (timeliness of care) from the benefit about patients getting care

changed.item: Original says each no-show is an untreated patient and a slot someone else could have used. The edit says each prevented no-show 'means someone else gets the care they need.' That shifts the beneficiary: preventing a no-show means the scheduled patient gets treated, not someone else.
'The change was simple' became 'All we did was', which more strongly asserts that text reminders were the sole cause of the reduction
